newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital market closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital market closing report.

text.p: French bonds wrapped up a week-long rally with the December futures contract just shy of yet another high struck on Friday after U.S. payroll data stunned the market and sent U.S. and European debt soaring.
The market is geared up for a further advance next week, traders and analysts said.
"We're really in a bull market now. It would take something really big to change sentiment," said one bond trader at a French bank.

One note of caution from bond analyst Nathalie Fillet at Paribas was that the rise in the U.S. September earnings component -- up six cents versus a forecast two cents -- could limit the magnitude of next week's advance.
The big figure was the shock fall of 40,000 in September non-farm payrolls, against expectations of a rise of 166,000.

On the heels of U.S. Treasury bonds, the December bond future leapt to a new contract high, the sixth in eight sessions and in the cash market the yield on 6.50 OAT due 2006 slid to 5.96, its lowest point since February 17, 1994.

PIBOR interest rate futures also gained from the bond future's momentum, with the December contract turning positive and gains of six, seven and nine basis points respectively for the June, September and December 1997 contracts.
"People are on a curve flattening play," said one PIBOR trader at a French brokerage.
Looking to next week, one trader said a spate of fresh economic data abroad and in France was unlikely to upset the trend set this week in the bond market.
"A lot of investors are underweight -- the more the movement keeps going the stronger the reaction gets," said the trader.

The monthly OAT auction this week provided further proof of strong demand for French debt, with the Treasury selling 20.297 billion francs of OATs on Thursday after originally saying it planned to sell between 16 and 18 billion.
It also sold more than 20 billion in the September auction after originally announcing 16 to 18 billion francs.
French data next week includes the September household survey and revised second-quarter GDP figures on Thursday, as well as provisional September consumer prices on Friday.
German unemployment figures come on Tuesday and the big U.S. figures on Friday are producer and retail prices.
